question: What does HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard markup language for creating web pages.

question: Which HTML element represents the root of an HTML document?
explanation: The <html> element represents the root of an HTML document, enclosing all other elements.

question: Which tag contains metadata, document title, and links to stylesheets?
explanation: The <head> tag contains machine-readable metadata and links to styles, scripts, and fonts.

question: Which tag contains the visible rendered content of a web page?
explanation: The <body> element contains all visible parts of an HTML document rendered by the browser.

question: What is the standard document type declaration for HTML5?
explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> is the concise HTML5 doctype declaration informing browsers of the document type.

question: Which HTML element defines the title shown on the browser tab?
explanation: The <title> element inside <head> sets the title shown on the browser window or tab.

question: Which HTML tag is used for the largest, highest-priority heading?
explanation: <h1> represents the top-level section heading on a webpage.

question: How many standard heading levels (h1 to h?) exist in HTML?
explanation: HTML provides standard heading elements from <h1> (highest) to <h6> (lowest).

question: Which HTML tag creates a text paragraph?
explanation:
The

element defines a paragraph of text.

question: Which HTML tag inserts a single line break without starting a new paragraph?
explanation:
The
tag inserts a line break and is a self-closing void element.

question: Which HTML element creates a thematic break or horizontal divider line?
explanation: The <hr> tag represents a thematic break between paragraphs or content sections.

question: Which attribute specifies the target URL for a hyperlink anchor tag (<a>)?
explanation: The href (Hypertext REFerence) attribute specifies the destination URL of a link.

question: Which attribute causes a link to open in a new browser tab or window?
explanation: target="_blank" directs the browser to open the hyperlink in a new browsing context (tab).

question: Which tag is used to embed an image into an HTML page?
explanation: The tag embeds an image resource into the document.

question: Which attribute provides alternative text for accessibility and screen readers?
explanation: The alt attribute provides fallback alternative text when the image cannot be displayed and for screen readers.

question: Which attribute defines the path or URL of the image file?
explanation: The src attribute points to the image file's source URL or path.

question: Which tag creates an unordered, bulleted list in HTML?
explanation: <ul> defines an unordered list, rendered with bullet points by default.

question: Which tag creates an ordered, numbered list in HTML?
explanation: <ol> defines an ordered list, typically rendered with numerical indicators.

question: Which tag represents an individual item inside an ordered or unordered list?
explanation: <li> (List Item) is used inside <ul> and <ol> to define each entry.

question: What is an empty or void element in HTML?
options: An element that cannot have child nodes or a closing tag
An element with no text styling
explanation:
Void elements (like ,
,
, ) cannot have content or closing tags.

question: How do you write a comment in HTML?
explanation: HTML comments are written between <!-- and --> markers.

question: What does CSS stand for?
explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, used to format the visual presentation of web documents.

question: Which HTML tag is used to include an external CSS stylesheet?
explanation: <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> is used to link an external CSS file.

question: Which HTML element is used to define internal CSS rules in the document head?
explanation: The <style> tag embeds internal CSS rules directly within an HTML document's <head>.

question: Which attribute is used to apply inline CSS styles directly on an HTML element?
explanation: The inline style attribute allows applying CSS declarations directly to an HTML element.

question: What character is used to separate CSS property declarations within a rule block?
explanation: CSS property declarations inside a declaration block must be separated by semicolons.

question: Which CSS property changes the text color of an element?
explanation: The color property sets the foreground color of an element's text content.

question: Which CSS property sets the background color of an element?
explanation: The background-color property specifies the solid fill color behind an element's content.

question: Which CSS property changes the size of the text font?
explanation: The font-size property specifies the dimension or scale of the font glyphs.

question: Which CSS property sets the typeface or font family of text?
explanation: The font-family property specifies a prioritized list of font family names for the selected element.

question: Which CSS property makes text bold?
explanation: font-weight controls the thickness or boldness of the font glyphs.

question: Which CSS property makes text italicized?
explanation: font-style: italic selects an italic version of the current typeface.

question: Which CSS property underlines text or removes default link underlines?
explanation: text-decoration: none removes underlines; text-decoration: underline adds them.

question: Which CSS property aligns text horizontally (left, center, right, justify)?
explanation: text-align specifies the horizontal alignment of inline-level content inside a block.

question: What symbol is used to select an element by its HTML 'id' in CSS?
explanation: The # symbol denotes an ID selector in CSS, e.g. #header.

question: What symbol is used to select an element by its HTML 'class' in CSS?
explanation: The period (.) denotes a class selector in CSS, e.g. .btn.

question: What symbol represents the universal selector in CSS that matches every element?
explanation: The asterisk (*) universal selector targets every element in the document tree.

question: How do you write a comment in CSS?
explanation: CSS comments are enclosed between /* and */.

question: Which CSS unit is an absolute measurement equivalent to 1/96th of an inch on standard displays?
explanation: Pixels (px) are standard absolute CSS screen units.

question: What is the default text color in most standard desktop browser user agent stylesheets?
explanation: Standard browser user agent stylesheets default to black text on a white canvas.

question:
Which CSS selector matches all

elements on a page?
explanation: A type (element) selector matches all HTML elements with the specified tag name.

question: Can multiple class names be applied to a single HTML element in the class attribute?
options: No, only one class is allowed
explanation: Multiple class names can be assigned to an element separated by whitespace (e.g. class="btn btn-primary").

question: What is JavaScript primarily designed to do in web development?
options: Provide dynamic interactivity, logic, and state manipulation in the browser
explanation: JavaScript is the high-level programming language that drives dynamic behavior and client logic on the web.

question: Which HTML tag is used to embed or reference client-side JavaScript code?
explanation: The <script> element embeds client-side scripts or references external script files via src.

question: Which attribute on the <script> tag specifies the path to an external JS file?
explanation: The src attribute defines the URL or relative path to the external JavaScript source file.

question: Which built-in JavaScript function prints messages to the browser developer console?
explanation: console.log() outputs informational messages to the browser's developer tools console.

question: Which popup dialog method displays a modal message with an OK button in the browser?
explanation: window.alert() displays a blocking modal dialog with a message and an OK button.

question: Which popup method prompts the user for text input and returns the entered string?
explanation: window.prompt() opens a dialog with a text field asking the user for input.

question: Which popup method displays a dialog with OK and Cancel buttons returning a boolean?
explanation: window.confirm() displays an OK/Cancel dialog returning true if OK is pressed, false otherwise.

question: How do you write a single-line comment in JavaScript?
explanation: In JavaScript, double slashes (//) denote a single-line comment.

question: How do you write a multi-line comment in JavaScript?
explanation: Multi-line comments in JavaScript start with /* and end with */.

question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
explanation: let declares a block-scoped local variable that can be subsequently reassigned.

question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
explanation: const declares an immutable block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned after initialization.

question: Which legacy keyword declares a function-scoped or globally-scoped variable?
explanation: var was the original ES5 variable declaration keyword, with function scope rather than block scope.

question: What data type is the value true or false in JavaScript?
explanation: Boolean represents logical entities having one of two values: true or false.

question: What data type represents textual data enclosed in quotes in JavaScript?
explanation: Strings represent sequences of UTF-16 code units enclosed in single, double, or backtick quotes.

question: What data type represents both integers and floating-point numbers in standard JavaScript?
explanation: In JavaScript, the Number type represents IEEE 754 double-precision 64-bit floating-point numbers.

question: What primitive value represents an uninitialized or absent variable binding?
explanation: undefined indicates that a variable has been declared but not yet assigned any value.

question: What special primitive value explicitly represents the intentional absence of any object value?
explanation: null is a primitive value representing the intentional absence of any object identity.

question: Which operator returns a string indicating the data type of an operand?
explanation: The typeof operator evaluates the type of an unevaluated operand and returns a descriptive string.

question: What does typeof 42 return?
explanation: typeof 42 evaluates to the string "number".

question: What does typeof "Hello" return?
explanation: typeof "Hello" evaluates to the string "string".

question: What is the statement terminator symbol commonly used in JavaScript?
explanation: Semicolons are standard statement terminators in JavaScript, though automatic semicolon insertion (ASI) exists.

question: Which tag defines the character encoding for an HTML5 document in <head>?
explanation: <meta charset="UTF-8"> informs the browser parser to decode document bytes using UTF-8 encoding.

question: What does the viewport meta tag (<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">) control?
options: The browser viewport dimensions and initial zoom level on mobile devices
The screen resolution of server logs
The maximum window size of desktop displays
explanation: The viewport meta tag ensures the page adapts its layout width to the mobile device screen width.

question: Which HTML tag is used to create a clickable button?
explanation: The <button> element represents a clickable button control.

question: What is the default type attribute value for a <button> inside an HTML <form>?
explanation: By default, a <button> element inside a form defaults to type="submit", submitting the form when clicked.

question: Which HTML tag is used to emphasize text, traditionally rendered in italics?
explanation: <em> represents semantic stress emphasis, which alters the sentence meaning and screen reader inflection.

question: Which HTML tag represents strong importance, seriousness, or urgency, traditionally rendered in bold?
explanation: <strong> indicates strong semantic importance for its contents, contrasting with pure visual bolding (<b>).

question: What is the semantic difference between <b> and <strong> in modern HTML5?
options: <b> is deprecated and strictly forbidden in HTML5
There is no difference; they are exact aliases
<strong> implies semantic importance/urgency, while <b> represents stylistic offset without special importance
explanation: <strong> conveys semantic importance for assistive tech, while <b> stylistically offsets text without added importance.

question: What is the semantic difference between <i> and <em> in modern HTML5?
options: <em> conveys vocal stress emphasis; <i> represents idiomatic text, technical terms, or thoughts without emphasis
<i> can only be used for icons
explanation: <em> conveys semantic stress emphasis altering spoken tone; <i> represents text in an alternate voice or mood.

question: Which tag is used to mark deleted or struck-through text in an HTML document?
explanation: <del> semantically represents a range of text that has been deleted from a document.

question: Which tag is used to represent inserted or newly added text?
explanation: <ins> represents an addition to the document, frequently styled with an underline.

question: Which tag highlights or marks text of relevance in another context?
explanation: The <mark> element represents text marked or highlighted for reference purposes.

question: Which tag represents small print such as copyright and legal notices?
explanation: The <small> element semantically represents side comments and small print, like copyright notices.

question: Which tag represents subscript text (e.g., in chemical formulas like H2O)?
explanation: <sub> specifies subscript text, positioned slightly lower than the baseline.

question: Which tag represents superscript text (e.g., exponents like x2)?
explanation: <sup> specifies superscript text, positioned slightly higher than the baseline.

question: Which tag is used to embed an abbreviation or acronym, optionally using the title attribute for its expansion?
explanation: <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr> provides an expansion for abbreviations.

question: Which tag is used to format computer code snippets in monospace text?
explanation: The <code> tag marks computer code fragments in inline content.

question: Which tag preserves whitespace, line breaks, and indentation exactly as typed?
explanation: The <pre> (preformatted) element displays text in a fixed-width font preserving whitespace and line breaks.

question: Which tag is used for longer block quotations cited from another source?
explanation: <blockquote> represents a section that is quoted from another source, typically indented by default.

question: Which tag is used for short inline quotations?
explanation: The <q> tag indicates that the enclosed text is an inline quotation, automatically inserting language-specific quote marks.

question: Which tag represents contact information for the author/owner of a document or article?
explanation: The <address> element supplies contact information for its nearest <article> or <body> ancestor.

question: Which attribute specifies the base URL for all relative URLs in an HTML document?
explanation: The <base> element specifies the base URL to use for all relative URLs contained within a document.

question: Which CSS selector targets an element that is a direct child of another element?
explanation: The child combinator (E > F) selects only elements F that are direct children of parent E.

question: Which CSS selector targets an element that is any descendant (child, grandchild, etc.) of another element?
explanation: A whitespace character between selectors (E F) matches F wherever it occurs inside E.

question: Which CSS selector matches an element that immediately follows another element sharing the same parent?
explanation: The adjacent sibling combinator (E + F) selects F only if it directly follows E.

question: Which CSS selector matches all sibling elements that follow another element under the same parent?
explanation: The general sibling combinator (E ~ F) selects all siblings F that appear after E.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element when the user points to it with a cursor device?
explanation: The :hover pseudo-class applies when the user interacts with an element using a pointing device without activating it.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element currently being activated or clicked by the user?
explanation: The :active pseudo-class represents the state while the element is being pressed or clicked by the user.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an interactive element (like an <input>) that has keyboard or pointer focus?
explanation: The :focus pseudo-class matches when an element has received focus, such as clicking an input field.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class applies styles when an element receives focus specifically via keyboard navigation?
explanation: :focus-visible provides focus rings only when navigating via keyboard rather than mouse clicks.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class applies to a parent container whenever any of its descendant elements has focus?
explanation: :focus-within matches an element if the element itself or any of its descendants matches :focus.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches a link that has already been visited in browser history?
explanation: :visited matches hyperlinks that the user has previously opened in their browser history.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an unvisited hyperlink?
explanation: :link targets unvisited anchor tags that possess an href attribute.

question: What is the standard mnemonic order recommended for styling anchor pseudo-classes in CSS?
explanation: To ensure correct cascade overriding, link pseudo-classes should be declared in the order :link, :visited, :hover, :active (Love-Hate).

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element that is the first child of its parent?
explanation: :first-child matches an element if it is the very first child node inside its parent.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element that is the last child of its parent?
explanation: :last-child matches an element if it is the final child element inside its parent.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element that is the only child of its parent?
explanation: :only-child matches an element that has no siblings.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class selects elements based on an algebraic formula or index (e.g. 2n+1)?
explanation: :nth-child(an+b) matches elements based on their numeric position among siblings.

question: Which CSS selector selects every even child element?
explanation: :nth-child(even) or :nth-child(2n) targets the 2nd, 4th, 6th, etc. children.

question: Which CSS selector selects every odd child element?
explanation: :nth-child(odd) or :nth-child(2n+1) targets the 1st, 3rd, 5th, etc. children.

question: How does :nth-of-type(n) differ from :nth-child(n)?
options: :nth-of-type counts only siblings with the exact same HTML tag name
explanation: :nth-of-type matches elements of a specific tag type among siblings, ignoring different element types.

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches an element whose ID matches the current URL fragment identifier (hash)?
explanation: The :target pseudo-class represents a unique element with an ID matching the URL's fragment identifier (#section).

question: Which CSS pseudo-class matches elements that have no children at all (including text nodes)?
explanation: :empty matches elements that contain no children (neither element nodes nor text/whitespace).

question: What happens if you attempt to reassign a variable declared with const?
options: The engine creates a second variable
A TypeError is thrown at runtime
explanation: Reassigning a const binding results in a TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.

question: Can properties of an object declared with const be modified or added?
options: No, const deeply freezes the entire object structure
Yes, const prevents reassigning the variable identifier, not mutating the object's properties
explanation: const creates an immutable variable binding to the object reference, but does not make the object itself immutable.

question: What is the scope of a variable declared with var?
options: Function-scoped (or globally scoped if outside a function)
explanation: var variables are scoped to the execution context of the enclosing function, ignoring block curly braces.

question: What is the scope of variables declared with let and const?
explanation: let and const are block-scoped, existing only within the curly braces {} in which they are declared.

question: What is variable hoisting in JavaScript?
options: Variables are automatically converted to strings
Variables are hoisted to external server memory
Variables are deleted at compile time
Variable and function declarations are processed by the engine before code execution begins
explanation: Hoisting is the JavaScript engine's behavior of reserving memory for declarations prior to code execution.

question: What value does a hoisted var variable have when accessed before its declaration line?
explanation: var declarations are hoisted and initialized with undefined, allowing access prior to declaration without a ReferenceError.

question: What happens if you access a let or const variable before its line of declaration?
options: A ReferenceError is thrown due to the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)
explanation: Accessing let or const before declaration throws ReferenceError because the variable is in the Temporal Dead Zone.

question: What is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) in JavaScript?
options: The time spent during garbage collection
The period between entering block scope and the variable declaration where access is prohibited
The time an asynchronous promise waits to resolve
explanation: The TDZ begins when execution enters the enclosing scope and ends when the variable's declaration statement is evaluated.

question: What is the result of typeof null in JavaScript?
explanation: typeof null evaluates to "object" due to a legacy bug in the original 1995 JavaScript implementation that was kept for web compatibility.

question: What primitive value is returned when an arithmetic operation produces an invalid number (e.g. Math.sqrt(-1))?
explanation: NaN (Not-a-Number) represents a computational result that is not a valid mathematical number.

question: What is the typeof NaN?
explanation: NaN is technically a value belonging to the IEEE 754 Number type, so typeof NaN evaluates to "number".

question: How can you reliably determine if a value is NaN without coercion bugs?
explanation: Number.isNaN(value) checks strictly if the value is NaN without attempting implicit type coercion (unlike global isNaN).

question: Why does NaN === NaN evaluate to false?
options: According to IEEE 754, NaN is not equal to any value, including itself
NaN is a dynamic object pointer
explanation: IEEE 754 specification defines that NaN is unequal to all values, including NaN itself.

question: Which primitive data type was introduced in ES6 to create unique, anonymous identifier keys?
explanation: Symbol creates unique, immutable primitives used primarily as collision-free object property keys.

question: Which primitive type was introduced in ES2020 to represent arbitrary-precision integers?
explanation: BigInt allows safely storing and operating on integers beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53 - 1).

question: How do you create a BigInt literal in JavaScript?
options: Wrap in double quotes with B prefix
explanation: Appending 'n' to the end of an integer literal creates a BigInt primitive.

question: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: == performs type coercion before comparison; === checks both value and type strictly without coercion
explanation: The strict equality operator (===) checks value and type without performing implicit type conversion.

question: What does 0 == false evaluate to?
explanation: With abstract equality (==), Boolean false is coerced to Number 0, making 0 == 0 evaluate to true.

question: What does 0 === false evaluate to?
explanation: With strict equality (===), 0 (number) and false (boolean) have different types, evaluating directly to false.

question: What does "5" + 2 evaluate to in JavaScript?
explanation: The binary + operator performs string concatenation when either operand is a string, resulting in "52".

question: What does "5" - 2 evaluate to in JavaScript?
explanation: The subtraction operator (-) only operates on numbers, coercing string "5" to number 5 and calculating 5 - 2 = 3.

question: Which anchor href format creates a clickable email link that launches the default mail client?
explanation: mailto: is the standard URI scheme for initiating email composition in the user's default client.

question: Which anchor href format initiates a phone call on mobile devices?
explanation: tel: URI scheme triggers telephony systems or dialing prompts on compatible devices.

question: Which anchor href value scrolls the viewport smoothly to an element with id="features" on the same page?
explanation: A hash followed by an element ID (#id) targets that fragment identifier within the current document.

question: Which attribute on an anchor tag prompts the browser to download the linked file instead of navigating to it?
explanation: The download attribute instructs the browser to download the URL rather than navigating to it.

question: When using target="_blank" on external links, which rel attribute combination is essential for security and performance?
explanation: noopener prevents the new page from accessing window.opener, preventing tab-nabbing security vulnerabilities.

question: Which tag pairs an image or illustration with an optional explanatory caption?
explanation: <figure> encapsulates self-contained media, and <figcaption> provides its semantic caption.

question: Can <figcaption> be placed as the first child inside a <figure> element?
options: No, it must always be at the very bottom
No, it must be outside the figure
Yes, <figcaption> can be either the first or last child of a <figure>

question: Which HTML5 element provides responsive image switching based on device pixel ratio or media queries?
explanation: The element wraps multiple elements and an fallback for responsive art direction.

question: Which attribute on the or tag defines a comma-separated list of image URLs and widths (e.g. 1x, 2x or 300w)?
explanation: srcset allows specifying multiple image resource candidates with pixel density or width descriptors.

question: Which attribute on specifies layout slot sizes corresponding to media conditions for srcset selection?
explanation: The sizes attribute tells the browser what width the image will occupy at specific viewport queries.

question: Which modern attribute on enables native browser lazy loading of offscreen images?
explanation: loading="lazy" instructs the browser to defer fetching the image until it nears the visible viewport.

question: Which HTML tag defines a client-side clickable image map with coordinate areas?
explanation: The <map> tag contains <area> definitions establishing clickable geometric hotspots on an image.

question: Which tag defines the clickable regions (rect, circle, poly) inside an image <map>?
explanation: <area> elements define the clickable geometric shapes and coordinates within an image map.

question: Which tag creates a description/definition list in HTML?
explanation: <dl> defines a description list consisting of term (<dt>) and description (<dd>) groupings.

question: Which tag represents a term or name inside an HTML description list (<dl>)?
explanation: <dt> (Description Term) specifies the name or term in a description list.

question: Which tag provides the definition or description of a term inside a description list (<dl>)?
explanation: <dd> (Description Details) provides the explanation or value corresponding to preceding <dt> terms.

question: Can a single <dt> term have multiple associated <dd> descriptions in valid HTML?
options: No, only one <dd> per <dt> is allowed
Yes, a term can have multiple descriptions
explanation: HTML specification allows multiple <dd> elements to provide multiple definitions for a single <dt> term.

question: Which attribute specifies whether an HTML element's text content is directly editable by the user in the browser?
explanation: contenteditable="true" makes any HTML element's inner text directly editable by the user.

question: Which attribute specifies the tab order sequence of elements when navigating with the keyboard?
explanation: tabindex specifies the sequential tab order position of an element for keyboard accessibility.

question: What does tabindex="-1" do to an element?
options: Hides the element from screen readers
Moves it to the top of the tab sequence
Removes it from the keyboard tab sequence, but allows programmatic focus via element.focus()
explanation: tabindex="-1" takes the element out of regular tab navigation, while keeping it focusable via script.

question: What does tabindex="0" do to an element?
options: Prevents the element from receiving focus
Makes the element the first focused item on load
Places the element into the natural document keyboard navigation order
explanation: tabindex="0" makes a normally non-focusable element focusable in natural DOM tree order.

question: What are the four components of the standard CSS Box Model, from the inside out?
explanation: The standard CSS box model consists of Content area, followed by Padding, Border, and finally outer Margin.

question: Which CSS Box Model component represents the space immediately inside the border, surrounding content?
explanation: Padding is the transparent space between an element's content and its border.

question: Which CSS Box Model component represents the space outside the border, separating it from adjacent elements?
explanation: Margin is the outermost transparent space separating the element from neighboring elements.

question: What is the default value of the box-sizing property in CSS?
explanation: By default, box-sizing is content-box, meaning width and height apply only to content, excluding padding and borders.

question: When box-sizing: border-box is applied, what does the width property include?
explanation: border-box ensures the specified width and height include padding and borders, avoiding box dimension expansion.

question: What phenomenon occurs when the vertical margins of two adjacent block elements overlap into a single margin?
explanation: Margin collapsing merges adjacent vertical block margins into a single margin equal to the largest individual margin.

question: Do horizontal (left and right) margins ever collapse in standard CSS?
explanation: In standard CSS layout, horizontal margins never collapse; only vertical margins collapse.

question: Which CSS property is a shorthand for margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom, and margin-left?
explanation: The margin shorthand sets margins in clockwise order: top, right, bottom, left.

question: In margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px;, what is the value of margin-right?
explanation: Clockwise shorthand order is Top (10px), Right (20px), Bottom (30px), Left (40px).

question: In margin: 10px 20px;, what are the top/bottom and left/right margin values respectively?
explanation: Two-value shorthand assigns the first value to Top/Bottom and the second value to Left/Right.

question: How do you horizontally center a block element with a fixed width inside its parent?
explanation: Setting margin-left and margin-right to auto distributes available horizontal space equally, centering the block.

question: Which CSS property sets the width of an element's border?
explanation: border-width specifies the thickness of all four borders of an element.

question: Which CSS property sets the visual style of a border (solid, dashed, dotted, none)?
explanation: border-style specifies the line style; without a border-style (which defaults to none), no border renders.

question: Which CSS property rounds the corners of an element's outer border edge?
explanation: border-radius defines the curvature radii of an element's corners.

question: How do you make a square element render as a perfect circle using CSS?
explanation: Setting border-radius: 50% on an element with equal width and height produces a circle.

question: What is the difference between an outline and a border in CSS?
options: Outlines do not take up layout space and do not affect document flow
explanation: Outlines are drawn outside the border edge without consuming box model layout dimensions.

question: Which property sets an outline around an element without affecting its dimensions?
explanation: outline draws a line around the exterior of elements outside the border edge.

question: Which CSS property adds shadow effects around an element's frame?
explanation: box-shadow casts drop shadows or inner shadows from an element's frame.

question: In box-shadow: 2px 4px 6px #000;, what does the third length value (6px) represent?
explanation: box-shadow arguments are: horizontal offset (2px), vertical offset (4px), blur radius (6px), and color (#000).

question: Can box-shadow accept an inset keyword to place the shadow inside the frame?
options: Yes, placing 'inset' creates an inner shadow
explanation: Adding the inset keyword draws the shadow inside the element's border box.

question: Which CSS property adds shadow effects specifically to text glyphs?
explanation: text-shadow applies one or more shadow effects directly to text characters.

question: What does the exponentiation operator (**) do in modern JavaScript?
options: Raises the first operand to the power of the second operand (e.g. 2 ** 3 = 8)
explanation: The ** operator computes exponentiation equivalent to Math.pow(x, y).

question: What does the modulus remainder operator (%) return?
options: The integer remainder of dividing the left operand by the right operand
explanation: The % operator returns the remainder left over when one operand is divided by another.

question: What does the post-increment operator (x++) return?
options: The value before incrementing, then increases the variable by 1
Adds 1 to x without returning anything
explanation: Post-increment (x++) evaluates to the current operand value before incrementing it.

question: What does the pre-increment operator (++x) return?
options: Increments the variable by 1 first, then returns the new value
explanation: Pre-increment (++x) increments the variable first and evaluates to the resulting updated value.

question: What does the logical AND operator (&&) return in JavaScript short-circuit evaluation?
options: The first falsy operand, or the last operand if all are truthy
explanation: && evaluates operands left-to-right, returning immediately upon finding the first falsy value.

question: What does the logical OR operator (||) return in JavaScript short-circuit evaluation?
options: The first truthy operand, or the last operand if all are falsy
explanation: || returns the first truthy operand encountered, short-circuiting remaining evaluations.

question: What does the nullish coalescing operator (??) do?
options: Returns the right-hand operand only if the left operand is null or undefined
Returns right operand if left operand is any falsy value (including 0 and "")
explanation: ?? returns its right-hand operand only when its left-hand operand evaluates strictly to null or undefined.

question: What does 0 ?? 42 evaluate to in JavaScript?
explanation: Because 0 is neither null nor undefined, ?? preserves 0, unlike || which would treat 0 as falsy and return 42.

question: What does false ?? true evaluate to?
explanation: false is not nullish (neither null nor undefined), so ?? preserves false.

question: What does null ?? "fallback" evaluate to?
explanation: Since the left operand is null, ?? returns the fallback right operand.

question: What does the logical NOT operator (!) do to an operand?
options: Inverts truthiness, returning false for truthy values and true for falsy values
explanation: The unary ! operator coerces its operand to boolean and negates it.

question: What does the double NOT operator (!!) do to an operand?
options: Explicitly coerces the operand to its boolean equivalent
explanation: !! (double exclamation) is an idiom used to explicitly cast any value to a true/false boolean.

question: Which of the following is considered falsy in JavaScript?
explanation: The 8 standard falsy values in JS are: false, 0, -0, 0n, "", null, undefined, and NaN.

question: Is an empty array [] truthy or falsy in JavaScript?
explanation: All objects and arrays in JavaScript are truthy, even empty ones ([] and {}).

question: Is an empty object {} truthy or falsy in JavaScript?
explanation: All object instances evaluate to truthy in boolean contexts.

question: Is the string "0" truthy or falsy in JavaScript?
explanation: Non-empty strings are always truthy in JavaScript, including "0" and "false".

question: What does the optional chaining operator (?.) do?
options: Checks if an array has items
Safely accesses nested properties without throwing an error if a reference is null or undefined
explanation: ?. evaluates to undefined instead of throwing a TypeError if the left reference is nullish.

question: What does user?.profile?.name evaluate to if user is null?
explanation: Optional chaining short-circuits at user?, immediately returning undefined.

question: Can optional chaining be used for function calls (e.g. callback?.())?
options: No, optional chaining only works on properties
Yes, it safely invokes the function only if it is not null or undefined
explanation: fn?.() executes the function if fn exists and is not null/undefined; otherwise it evaluates to undefined.

question: What is the ternary conditional operator syntax in JavaScript?
explanation: The ternary operator is the only JS operator taking three operands: condition ? trueExpr : falseExpr.

question: What does true ? "Yes" : "No" evaluate to?
explanation: The condition is truthy, so the ternary expression evaluates to the second operand ("Yes").

question: Which HTML element is used to collect user inputs in an interactive form container?
explanation: The <form> element encapsulates controls for collecting and submitting user data.

question: Which <form> attribute specifies the HTTP method (GET or POST) used to submit data?
explanation: The method attribute defines whether the form sends an HTTP GET or POST request.

question: Which <form> attribute specifies the endpoint URL where form data is sent upon submission?
explanation: The action attribute specifies the destination URL that processes the submitted data.

question: What is the default HTTP method for an HTML <form> if the method attribute is omitted?
explanation: If omitted, forms default to the GET method, appending form values as query parameters to the action URL.

question: How does a form submission using GET differ from POST?
options: GET is encrypted while POST is plain text
GET appends data to the URL query string; POST sends data in the HTTP request body
explanation: GET encodes parameters directly in the URL bar, whereas POST transmits data inside the request payload body.

question: Which attribute specifies the MIME encoding type when uploading files via a <form>?
explanation: Uploading binary files requires setting enctype="multipart/form-data" on the form.

question: Which tag pairs a textual caption with a form control for accessibility and clickability?
explanation: <label> provides an accessible text description for an input control.

question: How do you associate a <label> with a specific <input> element?
options: Set the label's 'for' attribute to match the input's 'id' attribute
Set the label's 'name' to match the input
Place them in the same class
explanation: Matching <label for="user-id"> with <input id="user-id"> associates them semantically for screen readers and click targeting.

question: What happens when a user clicks on an associated <label> element?
options: The browser automatically focuses or toggles the linked input element
explanation: Clicking an associated label shifts keyboard focus to the input or toggles checkboxes/radio buttons.

question: Which <input> type attribute value masks characters for secure password entry?
explanation: type="password" obscures entered text with bullets or asterisks.

question: Which <input> type attribute value provides an on-screen email keyboard on mobile and performs basic email syntax validation?
explanation: type="email" validates email format and displays keyboard layouts optimized with '@' on mobile.

question: Which <input> type creates a square toggle box allowing multiple choices among options?
explanation: type="checkbox" allows users to select zero, one, or multiple independent choices.

question: Which <input> type creates circular buttons where only one option in a group can be selected?
explanation: Radio buttons grouped with the same name attribute only allow a single selection at a time.

question: How do you group multiple radio buttons together so that selecting one deselects the others?
options: Give all radio buttons in the group the exact same name attribute
explanation: Radio buttons sharing the same name attribute belong to a mutually exclusive group.

question: Which tag creates a multi-line text input field?
explanation: The <textarea> element provides a multi-line plain-text editing control.

question: Which tag creates a dropdown selection list in HTML?
explanation: The <select> element creates a drop-down list of choices.

question: Which tag defines an individual selectable item inside a <select> dropdown?
explanation: The <option> element defines options inside a <select> or <datalist>.

question: Which tag groups related options under a labeled heading inside a <select> dropdown?
explanation: <optgroup> groups related <option> elements within a dropdown menu with a non-selectable label.

question: Which tag provides a predefined 'autocomplete' list of suggestions for an <input> element?
explanation: <datalist> contains <option> suggestions bound to an input via the input's list attribute.

question: Which attribute specifies hint text displayed inside an empty input field before user input?
explanation: The placeholder attribute displays a short hint intended to aid the user when the field is empty.

question: Which boolean attribute indicates that an input field must be filled out before submitting the form?
explanation: The required attribute prevents form submission if the input field is left empty.

question: Which CSS property sets the background image of an element?
explanation: background-image specifies one or more background images on an element using url().

question: How do you prevent a background image from repeating across the element surface?
explanation: background-repeat: no-repeat prevents the image from tiling horizontally or vertically.

question: Which background-size value scales the image to completely fill the container, cropping edges if needed?
explanation: cover scales the background image to ensure the entire background area is covered, cropping if aspect ratios differ.

question: Which background-size value scales the image to fit entirely within the container without cropping?
explanation: contain scales the image to the largest size such that both its width and height fit inside the container.

question: Which CSS property fixes the background image in place relative to the viewport so it does not scroll with content?
explanation: background-attachment: fixed keeps the background image stationary during page scrolling.

question: Which CSS property sets the initial horizontal and vertical position of a background image?
explanation: background-position sets the starting position (e.g. center center, top right) of each background image.

question: Which CSS unit is relative to the font-size of the element itself (or its parent for font-size)?
explanation: The em unit is relative to the font-size of the current element (or inherited font-size).

question: Which CSS unit is always relative to the font-size of the root (<html>) element?
explanation: rem (root em) is always relative to the font-size of the root <html> element (usually 16px by default).

question: If the root HTML font size is 16px, what pixel value does 1.5rem equal?
Which CSS unit represents 1% of the viewport width?
explanation: 1vw equals 1 percent of the width of the current browser viewport.

question: Which CSS unit represents 1% of the viewport height?
explanation: 1vh equals 1 percent of the height of the browser viewport.

question: Which modern CSS viewport units adapt accurately to dynamic mobile browser address bars?
explanation: Dynamic (dvh), Small (svh), and Large (lvh) viewport units account for mobile UI address bar expansion.

question: Which CSS color model defines colors using red, green, blue, and alpha transparency channels?
explanation: rgba(r, g, b, a) defines color channels alongside an alpha channel from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque).

question: Which CSS color model defines colors using Hue (degrees), Saturation (%), and Lightness (%)?
explanation: hsl(hue, saturation, lightness) provides an intuitive color model based on the color wheel.

question: What does the hex color code #FFFFFF represent?
explanation: #FFFFFF corresponds to full intensity red, green, and blue, producing pure white.

question: What does the hex color code #000000 represent?
explanation: #000000 represents zero intensity across red, green, and blue, producing pure black.

question: What does opacity: 0.5; do to an element?
options: Makes the element and all its children 50% semi-transparent
explanation: The opacity property sets the transparency level of an element and all of its descendants together.

question: How does setting background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.5) differ from setting opacity: 0.5?
options: rgba only makes the background transparent without affecting child elements and text
explanation: rgba applies transparency solely to the background fill, preserving full opacity for text and children.

question: Which CSS property controls how an element handles content that exceeds its box dimensions?
explanation: overflow specifies what happens if content overflows an element's box (visible, hidden, scroll, auto).

question: What does overflow: hidden; do to content extending beyond the element boundary?
options: Moves overflow to the next line
Clips the overflowing content without providing scrollbars
explanation: overflow: hidden hides any child content extending past the element's padding box without scrollbars.

question: What does overflow: auto; do?
options: Adds scrollbars only if the content overflows the container dimensions
explanation: auto displays scrollbars dynamically only when content exceeds container boundaries.

question: Which control flow statement executes a code block only if a specified condition evaluates to truthy?
explanation: The if statement executes a block of code if its condition evaluates to true.

question: Which keyword provides an alternate code block when the initial 'if' condition is falsy?
explanation: The else clause executes when the preceding if condition is false.

question: Which control flow structure tests an expression against multiple case values using strict equality (===)?
explanation: The switch statement evaluates an expression against a series of case clauses using strict equality.

question: What keyword prevents execution from 'falling through' to the next case in a switch statement?
explanation: The break statement terminates the current switch case, preventing execution from continuing into subsequent cases.

question: What keyword provides a fallback case in a switch statement when no other case matches?
explanation: The default clause in a switch statement executes if none of the cases match the evaluated expression.

question: What happens if you omit the 'break' statement at the end of a matching switch case?
options: Execution continues down into the next case block regardless of whether that case matches (fall-through)
explanation: Omitting break results in fall-through behavior, where execution continues directly into the subsequent case.

question: Which loop executes a block of code repeatedly as long as a specified condition evaluates to true?
explanation: The while loop evaluates condition before each iteration, executing while truthy.

question: Which loop always executes its code block at least once before testing the condition?
explanation: The do...while loop tests its condition at the end of the loop, ensuring at least one guaranteed execution.

question: What are the three semicolon-separated expressions inside a standard 'for' loop header?
explanation: for (initialization; condition; update) controls execution across iterations.

question: What does the break statement do inside a loop?
options: Immediately terminates the loop and transfers control to the statement following the loop
explanation: break immediately aborts the loop, continuing execution outside the loop structure.

question: What does the continue statement do inside a loop?
options: Terminates the current iteration immediately and proceeds to the next iteration
explanation: continue halts execution of the current loop iteration and advances directly to the next cycle.

question: Which statement terminates a function execution and specifies a value to be returned to the function caller?
explanation: The return statement ends function execution and specifies the value delivered back to the caller.

question: What value does a JavaScript function return if it executes to completion without an explicit return statement?
explanation: Functions without a return statement implicitly evaluate to undefined upon completion.

question: How do you declare a standard named function in JavaScript?
explanation: The function declaration syntax defines a function with specified parameters and body.

question: Can a standard function declaration be invoked before its definition in the code file?
options: Yes, because function declarations are fully hoisted with their bodies
explanation: Function declarations are hoisted in their entirety, allowing them to be called prior to their line of definition.

question: What is a function expression in JavaScript?
options: Assigning a function to a variable (e.g. const fn = function() { ... })
explanation: A function expression creates a function object and assigns it to a variable binding.

question: Are function expressions hoisted in the same way as function declarations?
options: No, the variable binding is hoisted (as undefined if var, or TDZ if let/const), not the function body
explanation: Function expressions assigned to variables cannot be called before the assignment line executes.

question: What is an arrow function in ES6?
options: A function that only accepts numbers
A concise function syntax using the => token that lexically binds 'this'
explanation: Arrow functions provide concise syntax ((args) => expr) and inherit this from the surrounding lexical scope.

question: Do arrow functions have their own 'this' binding or 'arguments' object?
options: No, they inherit 'this' and 'arguments' from their parent enclosing lexical scope
explanation: Arrow functions do not bind their own this, arguments, super, or new.target.

question: What is an IIFE in JavaScript?
options: Immediately Invoked Function Expression (runs as soon as defined)
explanation: An IIFE ((function() { ... })()) is a function that executes immediately upon creation to create an isolated scope.

question: What is the purpose of "use strict"; at the top of a JavaScript file or function?
options: Enables Strict Mode, catching silent coding errors, eliminating with statements, and forbidding accidental globals
explanation: Strict Mode ("use strict";) enforces cleaner code by converting silent errors to throw exceptions and preventing bad syntax.

question: Which HTML tag defines a table container?
explanation: The <table> tag represents tabular data, presented in two or more dimensions.

question: Which HTML tag represents a table row?
explanation: <tr> (Table Row) defines a row of cells in a table.

question: Which HTML tag defines a table header cell, rendered bold and centered by default?
explanation: <th> (Table Header) defines a cell that contains header information for a column or row.

question: Which HTML tag defines a standard data cell in an HTML table?
explanation: <td> (Table Data) defines a standard data cell in an HTML table.

question: Which attribute merges a table cell across multiple horizontal columns?
explanation: colspan specifies the number of columns a cell should span horizontally.

question: Which attribute merges a table cell across multiple vertical rows?
explanation: rowspan specifies the number of rows a cell should span vertically.

question: Which tag groups the header content (title rows) in a table?
explanation: <thead> wraps the header rows of a table, separating headers from the body.

question: Which tag groups the main body content rows in an HTML table?
explanation: <tbody> encapsulates the main data rows in an HTML table.

question: Which tag groups the footer or summary row at the bottom of a table?
explanation: <tfoot> encapsulates summary rows (like totals) at the bottom of a table.

question: Which tag provides a title or caption for an entire table?
explanation: The <caption> element specifies the caption (or title) of a table and must be its first child.

question: Where must the <caption> tag be placed inside a <table> element?
explanation: In valid HTML, <caption> must be the first child element directly following <table>.

question: Which tag specifies column properties for each column within a <colgroup> in a table?
explanation: The <col> tag specifies column properties for each column in a <colgroup>.

question: Which tag groups one or more columns in a table for formatting purposes?
explanation: <colgroup> specifies a group of one or more columns in a table for styling.

question: Which attribute on a <th> element associates the header with a row, column, rowgroup, or colgroup?
explanation: The scope attribute (col, row, colgroup, rowgroup) makes tables accessible to screen readers.

question: Which CSS property merges adjacent table cell borders into a single continuous border?
explanation: border-collapse: collapse unites adjacent cell borders into a single shared rule line.

question: What is the default value of border-collapse in standard CSS table rendering?
explanation: By default, table cell borders are separate, rendered with border-spacing between them.

question: Which CSS property sets the distance between borders of adjacent cells when border-collapse is separate?
explanation: border-spacing specifies the distance between borders of adjacent cells in a separated table model.

question: Which attribute in legacy HTML (replaced by CSS) set the internal padding inside cells?
explanation: The legacy cellpadding attribute defined the space between cell wall and cell content.

question: Which legacy attribute (replaced by border-spacing in CSS) set the space between cells?
explanation: cellspacing defined space between table cells in older HTML versions.

question: Which CSS property controls whether an empty cell with no content renders borders in a separate border model?
explanation: empty-cells (show or hide) controls whether borders and backgrounds render on empty cells.

question: Which CSS property optimizes table rendering performance by locking column widths based on the first row?
explanation: table-layout: fixed calculates column widths from the first row and col tags, enabling fast rendering.

,

, and
?
explanation: Block-level elements generate a box that breaks onto a new line and takes up full available width by default.

question: What is the default display value of elements like <span>, <a>, <strong>, and <em>?
explanation: Inline elements flow alongside surrounding text and do not break onto a new line.

question: Can you set explicit width and height properties on a standard display: inline element?
options: Yes, width works but height does not
No, width and height have no effect on inline elements
explanation: In standard inline display, width and height declarations are ignored; dimensions are determined by content.

question: How do top and bottom padding/margins behave on a standard display: inline element?
options: They render visually but do not push surrounding vertical line boxes away
explanation: Vertical padding and margins on inline elements render over adjacent content without altering line box layout.

question: How does display: inline-block differ from display: inline?
options: inline-block breaks onto a new line
inline-block allows setting explicit width, height, and vertical margins while still flowing inline
explanation: inline-block formats an element as an inline flow item whose internal box respects width and height.

question: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
options: visibility: hidden removes element from DOM
display: none removes the element from page layout entirely; visibility: hidden hides it while preserving its space
explanation: display: none releases layout space; visibility: hidden renders a transparent gap reserving the box dimensions.

question: Does an element styled with display: none trigger screen reader speech by default?
options: Yes, screen readers always read it
No, display: none hides elements from sighted users and assistive screen readers alike
Only if it has an aria-label
explanation: display: none instructs user agents to omit the element entirely from the accessibility tree.

question: Which CSS property controls how white-space, tabs, and newlines inside an element are handled?
explanation: white-space (normal, nowrap, pre, pre-wrap, pre-line) governs whitespace and line breaking.

question: Which white-space value prevents text from wrapping to the next line completely?
explanation: white-space: nowrap collapses whitespace but suppresses automatic line breaking.

question: Which CSS property adds an ellipsis (...) when text overflows its container?
explanation: text-overflow: ellipsis clips overflowing text and displays an ellipsis glyph (...) at the boundary.

question: What combination of three CSS properties is required to create a single-line text ellipsis truncation?
options: display: inline; overflow: scroll; ellipsis: on;
text-overflow: ellipsis; word-break: break-all; width: auto;
white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
explanation: Truncating single-line text requires preventing wrap (nowrap), hiding overflow (hidden), and applying ellipsis.

question: Which CSS property forces long words or URLs without spaces to break onto the next line?
explanation: overflow-wrap: break-word allows unbroken strings to be separated across lines to prevent overflow.

question: Which CSS property sets the vertical distance between lines of text?
explanation: line-height sets the height of a line box, controlling the leading between baselines of text.

question: Why is a unitless number (e.g. line-height: 1.5) preferred over fixed pixels or percentages for line-height?
options: Unitless line-height renders faster in GPU
Child elements inherit the factor and scale line-height proportionally to their own font-size
explanation: Unitless line-height (1.5) acts as a multiplier, allowing child elements with different font sizes to scale correctly.

question: Which CSS property controls the horizontal spacing between text characters (tracking)?
explanation: letter-spacing adjusts the horizontal spacing between text characters.

question: Which CSS property controls the spacing between words in text?
explanation: word-spacing specifies the additional spacing between individual words.

question: Which CSS property controls the capitalization of text (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize)?
explanation: text-transform (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize) alters character casing visually without modifying DOM text.

question: Which CSS property controls the vertical alignment of an inline or table-cell element?
explanation: vertical-align (baseline, middle, top, bottom) positions inline-level and table-cell boxes vertically.

question: What is the default vertical-align value for inline elements and text?
explanation: By default, inline elements align to the baseline of their parent box.

question: Which property sets how text wraps around floating elements or shapes?
explanation: shape-outside defines a geometric boundary around which adjacent inline content wraps.

question: What does visibility: collapse do when applied to an HTML table row (<tr>)?
options: Hides the row and removes its height without recalculating entire table column widths
explanation: On table rows and columns, visibility: collapse removes them without forcing column width recalculation.

question: Which loop structure is designed specifically to iterate over the keys (property names) of an object?
explanation: for...in iterates over all enumerable string properties of an object, including inherited prototype properties.

question: Which loop structure was introduced in ES6 to iterate over values of iterable collections (Arrays, Strings, Maps, Sets)?
explanation: for...of iterates over the values produced by an iterable object's @@iterator method.

question: What happens if you use for...of on a plain JavaScript object ({ a: 1 }) without an iterator?
options: Throws a TypeError: object is not iterable
explanation: Plain objects are not iterable by default, so attempting for...of throws a TypeError.

question: How can you safely check if a variable is an Array in JavaScript?
explanation: Array.isArray() reliably detects arrays across execution realms, whereas typeof returns 'object'.

question: What does typeof [] evaluate to in JavaScript?
explanation: Arrays are specialized objects in JavaScript, so typeof [] returns "object".

question: How do you determine the number of elements in an array?
explanation: The length property reflects the number of elements present in an array.

question: Which array method appends one or more elements to the end of an array and returns the new length?
explanation: push() mutates the array by adding elements to the end and returns the updated array length.

question: Which array method removes the last element from an array and returns that element?
explanation: pop() removes the final element from an array and returns it, reducing array length by 1.

question: Which array method removes the first element from an array and returns that element?
explanation: shift() removes and returns the first element at index 0, shifting all subsequent elements down.

question: Which array method inserts one or more elements at the beginning of an array?
explanation: unshift() inserts elements at index 0, moving existing elements up, and returns the new length.

question: What is the performance difference between push/pop and shift/unshift on large arrays?
options: push/pop are O(1) operations, while shift/unshift are O(n) because all elements must be re-indexed
explanation: shift and unshift re-index every remaining element in memory, making them significantly slower on large arrays.

question: Which array method returns the first index at which a given element can be found, or -1 if not present?
explanation: indexOf(element) scans using strict equality (===) and returns the first matching index, or -1.

question: Which ES2016 array method determines whether an array includes a certain value, returning a boolean?
explanation: includes(value) returns true if the value is found, and properly handles NaN comparison (unlike indexOf).

question: Can array.includes(NaN) find NaN inside an array?
options: Yes, includes() utilizes the SameValueZero algorithm which matches NaN
No, NaN can never be found
explanation: Array.prototype.includes uses SameValueZero comparison, successfully detecting NaN values.

question: Which array method merges two or more arrays without mutating the existing arrays?
explanation: concat() returns a new array composed of the items from the original arrays without modifying them.

question: Which array method reverses an array in-place, mutating the original array?
explanation: reverse() mutates the original array by reversing its element sequence in place.

question: Which ES2023 array method returns a reversed copy of an array without mutating the original?
explanation: toReversed() produces a new reversed array, preserving the immutability of the source array.

question: Which array method joins all elements of an array into a single string separated by a specified delimiter?
explanation: join(separator) converts all array elements to strings and concatenates them with the separator.

question: What is the default separator used by array.join() if none is specified?
explanation: If no separator is passed, join() defaults to using a comma as the delimiter.

question: What does array.slice(start, end) do?
options: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of an array into a new array without mutating the original
explanation: slice(start, end) extracts elements up to (but not including) end into a new array without modifying source.

question: What happens if you assign a value to an array index beyond its current length (e.g. arr[100] = 'x' on an empty array)?
options: Creates a sparse array with empty slots (length becomes 101)
explanation: JavaScript creates a sparse array containing empty slots, automatically expanding length to index + 1.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents the primary introductory content or navigational banner of a page?
explanation: The <header> element contains introductory content or a set of navigational links.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents a major section of navigational links?
explanation: <nav> designates a section of major navigation links intended for site-wide navigation.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents the dominant, central content unique to the document body?
explanation: The <main> element represents the dominant content of the <body>; there should only be one non-hidden <main> per document.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents a self-contained, independently distributable composition (e.g. blog post, news item)?
explanation: <article> represents a complete, self-contained composition suitable for independent syndication.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents a generic standalone thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading?
explanation: <section> represents a standalone thematic section of a document, typically with an introductory heading.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents content tangentially related to surrounding content, often rendered as a sidebar?
explanation: <aside> marks content indirectly related to the main article, such as sidebars, glossaries, or callouts.

question: Which semantic HTML5 tag represents a footer for its nearest sectioning content, containing copyright or author data?
explanation: The <footer> element represents a footer for its nearest sectioning ancestor or the page root.

question: Which HTML5 tag represents a machine-readable date, time, or duration?
explanation: <time> represents a specific period in time, utilizing the datetime attribute for ISO-8601 strings.

question: Which attribute on the <time> tag provides a standardized machine-readable ISO date string?
explanation: datetime="2026-10-23T12:00:00Z" provides a machine-readable date timestamp for search engines and calendars.

question: Which HTML5 element creates a native toggleable disclosure widget with interactive hide/reveal behavior?
explanation: The <details> element creates an interactive widget that the user can open and close natively.

question: Which tag provides the visible summary or clickable label for a <details> disclosure element?
explanation: The <summary> element specifies a visible heading for the parent <details> disclosure box.

question: Which boolean attribute on a <details> element causes it to be expanded by default on page load?
explanation: The open attribute specifies that the details disclosure widget should be visible to the user.

question: Which native HTML5 element represents an interactive popup dialog or modal window?
explanation: <dialog> represents a dialog box, subwindow, or interactive modal component.

question: Which JavaScript method opens an HTML <dialog> as a backdrop-blocked modal window?
explanation: dialog.showModal() opens the dialog as a top-layer modal, inerting background elements and rendering ::backdrop.

question: Which JavaScript method closes an active HTML <dialog> element?
explanation: dialog.close() closes the dialog and removes it from the top layer.

question: Which tag defines client-side content that is not rendered on page load, but can be cloned and instantiated by JavaScript?
explanation: <template> holds inert HTML fragments that are not rendered until instantiated via script.

question: Which tag defines a placeholder inside a Web Component Shadow DOM where light DOM content is projected?
explanation: The <slot> element serves as an insertion point inside a shadow tree for external content projection.

question: Which tag represents the calculated result of a user calculation or form operation?
explanation: <output> represents the result of a calculation performed by client script or form interaction.

question: Which tag displays an indeterminate or determinate progress bar of a task?
explanation: <progress> represents the completion progress of a task with value and max attributes.

question: Which tag displays a scalar measurement within a known gauge range (e.g., disk usage, battery level)?
explanation: <meter> represents a scalar fractional value or gauge within a known range with min, max, low, high, and optimum attributes.

question: What is the fundamental difference between <progress> and <meter> in semantic HTML?
options: <progress> shows completion towards 100% of a task; <meter> measures a static value within a fixed range
explanation: <progress> communicates task completion progress; <meter> represents a scalar measurement (like disk usage).

question: What is the default value of the position property in CSS?
explanation: By default, elements are positioned statically in the normal document flow.

question: Do offset properties (top, right, bottom, left) or z-index affect an element with position: static?
options: Yes, they shift the element normally
No, top/right/bottom/left and z-index are completely ignored on static elements
explanation: Offset properties and z-index only apply to positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky).

question: How does position: relative behave?
options: Positions the element relative to its normal flow position, without moving surrounding layout flow
Positions relative to the browser window
explanation: position: relative offsets an element relative to where it would naturally be, reserving its original space in document flow.

question: How does position: absolute behave?
options: Positions relative to the screen viewport always
Reserves empty space in the flow
Positions relative to direct parent always
Removes element from document flow and positions it relative to its nearest positioned ancestor
explanation: position: absolute removes the element from flow, positioning relative to the nearest ancestor with position other than static.

question: What ancestor does an element with position: absolute position against if no ancestor is positioned?
explanation: If no positioned ancestor exists, an absolute element positions against the initial containing block.

question: How does position: fixed behave?
options: Removes element from document flow and positions it relative to the browser viewport, staying fixed during scrolling
explanation: position: fixed anchors the element relative to the viewport coordinate system, keeping it static during page scroll.

question: How does position: sticky behave?
options: Toggles between relative and fixed depending on scroll position relative to its scroll container
Locks element to bottom of screen
explanation: Sticky positioning behaves as relative within its parent until reaching a threshold offset, where it sticks like fixed.

question: Why might position: sticky fail to stick inside a container?
options: The element has no background color
An ancestor has overflow: hidden, overflow: auto, or overflow: scroll set
explanation: Setting overflow (other than visible) on an ancestor clips sticky positioning and prevents scrolling adhesion.

question: Which modern CSS property is shorthand for setting top, right, bottom, and left simultaneously?
explanation: inset: 0 is shorthand for top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0;.

question: How do you center an absolutely positioned element perfectly in both axes?
explanation: Translating -50% of the element's own dimensions offsets the 50% coordinate anchor to achieve perfect centering.

question: Which CSS property controls the 3D stacking order along the z-axis for positioned elements?
explanation: z-index specifies the stack level of positioned elements; higher numbers render in front of lower numbers.

question: What condition must be met for z-index to take effect on an element in standard CSS?
options: The element must be a positioned element (position other than static) or a flex/grid item
The element must have a border
The element must have overflow: hidden
explanation: z-index only applies to positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) or flex/grid child items.

question: What is a stacking context in CSS?
options: A layout mechanism in CSS Grid
A three-dimensional conceptual categorization of HTML elements along the z-axis relative to the user
explanation: A stacking context determines the rendering hierarchy in which elements are drawn along the screen's z-axis.

question: Which of the following creates a new stacking context on an element?
options: opacity less than 1, transform other than none, or filter other than none
explanation: Properties like opacity < 1, transform, filter, and will-change establish independent stacking contexts.

question: Can a child element with z-index: 9999 appear in front of an element outside its parent if the parent has z-index: 1?
options: No, child elements cannot escape their parent's stacking context
Only if position: fixed is used
explanation: A stacking context is self-contained; children are flattened into their parent's stack level relative to siblings.

question: Which CSS property tells the browser which properties an element will change, allowing ahead-of-time GPU optimizations?
explanation: will-change (e.g. will-change: transform) hints to browser rendering engines to prepare GPU resources.

question: Which property sets whether an element can be the target of pointer/mouse click events?
explanation: pointer-events: none makes an element completely click-through, allowing clicks to pass to elements beneath it.

question: Which CSS property customizes the mouse cursor displayed when hovering over an element?
explanation: cursor: pointer displays a hand pointer; cursor: not-allowed indicates disabled states.

question: Which CSS property controls whether user selection of text is enabled or disabled?
explanation: user-select: none prevents users from highlighting or selecting text on UI buttons and controls.

question: Which CSS property controls the aspect ratio of an element's box dimensions (e.g. 16 / 9)?
explanation: aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 defines a preferred aspect ratio for the box, maintaining proportions automatically.

question: Which CSS property determines how an or
explanation: object-fit specifies how replaced element contents (images/videos) scale within their box.

question: How do you define default parameter values in ES6 function signatures?
explanation: ES6 allows initializing formal parameters with default values directly in the function declaration header.

question: What triggers the evaluation of a default parameter expression in JavaScript?
options: Passing undefined or omitting the argument during function invocation
explanation: Default parameters only activate when the argument is undefined or completely omitted; null is treated as an explicit value.

question: Which ES6 syntax allows a function to accept an indefinite number of arguments as a real array?
explanation: Rest parameter syntax (...args) collects remaining arguments into a true Array instance.

question: Where must rest parameters (...args) be placed in a function parameter list?
options: As the very last parameter in the function signature
explanation: Rest parameters must be the final formal parameter in a function declaration; otherwise a SyntaxError is thrown.

question: How does the rest parameter (...args) differ from the legacy arguments object?
options: Rest parameters only work in Node.js
Rest parameters produce a real Array instance; arguments is an array-like object lacking array methods
explanation: Rest parameters generate genuine Array objects with map, filter, etc., whereas arguments lacks array prototype methods.

question: What is a Higher-Order Function in JavaScript?
options: A function with more than 10 lines of code
A function executed in server memory
A function that accepts another function as an argument, returns a function, or both
explanation: Higher-order functions operate on other functions by taking them as parameters or returning them.

question: What is a callback function in JavaScript?
options: A function that calls the browser window
A function passed as an argument to another function to be executed at a later time
explanation: A callback is a function supplied to another function, invoked when a specific event or task completes.

question: What is function currying?
options: Transforming a function with multiple arguments into a sequence of functions each taking a single argument
explanation: Currying translates f(a, b, c) into f(a)(b)(c), evaluating each argument sequentially.

question: What is a pure function in programming?
options: A function that produces identical output for identical inputs and causes no observable side effects
A function that only uses primitive types
A function defined in global scope
explanation: Pure functions have deterministic output and do not modify external state, network, or DOM (no side effects).

question: What is recursion in computer programming?
options: A function calling itself until a defined base case condition is met
explanation: Recursion occurs when a function solves subproblems by calling itself until reaching a termination base case.

question: What critical condition must every recursive function have to prevent infinite call stack overflow?
explanation: Without a base case, recursion continues indefinitely until exhausting call stack memory (Maximum call stack size exceeded).

question: What error is thrown when a recursive function overflows available call stack memory?
options: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
explanation: The engine throws a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded when function recursion exceeds stack limits.

question: What is an anonymous function in JavaScript?
